subject: Biotechnology
title: De-Extinction Ethics
description: A quick, practical guide to De-Extinction Ethics.

hook.text: Bring back the woolly mammoth — Colossal Biosciences says it can. But should we resurrect extinct species?

buildup.text: Ancient DNA from frozen specimens provides the blueprint — CRISPR edits cold-adapted genes into Asian elephant cells.

discovery.text: Proponents argue de-extinction restores ecosystem functions — mammoths could revive grasslands and slow Arctic permafrost thawing.

twist.text: Critics say de-extinction diverts funds from conserving living species — why resurrect the dead when the living need help?

climax.text: A resurrected mammoth is not a real mammoth — it is an elephant-mammoth hybrid with no mammoth culture or social knowledge.

punchline.text: Can we bring them back? Probably. Should we? That is the harder question.

quiz.question: Why would a de-extincted mammoth not truly be a woolly mammoth?
options: It would be too small to survive in cold climates
It would be a genetically engineered elephant-mammoth hybrid lacking the social behaviors and culture of real mammoths
Ancient mammoth DNA has degraded too much to provide any useful genetic information

details.summary: De-extinction uses biotechnology to revive extinct species by editing the genomes of close living relatives to express ancestral traits. Projects targeting the woolly mammoth and dodo raise profound ethical questions about ecological impact and resource allocation.
details.whyItMatters: De-extinction tests the limits of biotechnological power and responsibility. Should we resurrect species when thousands of living species face extinction? The debate forces society to weigh scientific capability against ecological wisdom.
takeaways: Gene editing of living relatives could recreate extinct species' traits
Critics argue resources should prioritize conserving endangered living species
Ecological roles of revived species in modern ecosystems are uncertain

faq.question: Could we really bring back the woolly mammoth?
faq.answer: Colossal Biosciences is editing Asian elephant cells to express mammoth traits like cold tolerance and dense hair. The result would be a mammoth-like elephant, not an exact replica. Full de-extinction is impossible because we lack complete mammoth genomes and social knowledge.

faq.question: Is de-extinction a responsible use of conservation resources?
faq.answer: Critics argue that billions spent on de-extinction could save thousands of endangered species. Proponents counter that it advances genetic rescue techniques applicable to living species and generates public interest and funding for conservation broadly.
